new_statements.rule_in_words: In the Seko languages (explicitly Seko Padang, Seko Tengah, Panasuan and Budong-Budong, described from the author's fieldwork), word stress falls on the penultimate syllable; consonant-initial possessive suffixes are stress-shifting, i.e. stress is recomputed on the suffixed word so it stays penultimate; a word-final long vowel does not attract stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for stress placement; the echo vowel -i of Seko Padang is described as non-stress-shifting (Seko Padang-specific). Budong-Budong is noted to have often lost final vowel length under Topoiyo/Mamuju influence, but nothing is said about its stress differing from the group pattern.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level synchronic statement covering all four Seko languages, not a Budong-Budong-specific description; word-level stress, illustrated with Seko Padang and Seko Tengah citation forms. The paper is a historical reconstruction whose section 2 is a first-hand synchronic phonology overview.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is a group-level generalisation over the four Seko languages (Seko Padang skx/seko1245, Seko Tengah sko, Panasuan psn/pana1305, Budong-Budong bdx/budo1241) by an SIL fieldworker who worked in the area; Budong-Budong (= Tangkou/Tongkou, the name used in the Japanese/ELPR literature) is explicitly included but not separately exemplified for stress. Laskowske notes Budong-Budong is a recent split from Panasuan and is under heavy Topoiyo/Mamuju contact influence (loss of final vowel length), so a language-specific confirmation (Manda et al. 2002 or Yamaguchi 2003) is desirable.

sources.note: Sec. 2 'Seko Synchronic Phonology', 2.1 'Overview of basic features' lists 'the common basic elements of the phonology of Seko languages' (Seko Padang, Seko Tengah, Panasuan, Budong-budong, from the author's own fieldwork): p.3 item 7 'Stress is penultimate.'; item 10 possessive suffixes are stress-shifting; 2.2 p.3 'Word stress does not shift, but remains penultimate' (re word-final long vowels; examples Seko Padang); vowel 'quickness' contrastive only in the stressed (penultimate) syllable. No Budong-Budong-specific stress data beyond the group statement.
